# Wave Laser fires from ship

## Headline

The beam weapons (Wave Laser and Mining Laser — both confirmed in scope, Q1 = A) currently render a **static polyline frozen at fire time**, so as the ship keeps flying during the beam's visible lifetime the beam's source end visibly detaches from the ship. The fix: each frame the beam's **source end tracks the ship's current position** while its **destination (the launch-resolved end point) stays fixed** — a purely visual change in the shared VFX seam.

## Problem statement

When the ship fires a beam weapon and keeps moving, the rendered beam stays anchored to the world position the ship occupied at the moment of firing rather than to the ship itself. With the ship's max speed around 175 px/s, a Wave Laser beam (visible 0.3 s) can drift up to ~50 px clear of the ship's nose while the beam is still on screen, so the beam visibly no longer "fires from the ship". The Mining Laser beam (visible 0.12 s) has the same static-polyline behaviour and is confirmed in scope (Q1 = A).

## Users

- **The player** — watches the ship fire the Wave Laser (and Mining Laser) while dodging; the beam should read as emanating from the ship's current position, never as floating in space where the ship was a moment ago.

**User stories:**

- As the player, when my ship fires a Wave Laser and I keep flying, the red beam's source end stays attached to my ship and follows it, while the beam's far end stays fixed at the point where it resolved — so the beam always visibly fires *from* my ship.
- As the player, when the Mining Laser is cutting an asteroid, its beam likewise stays connected to my ship as it drifts, not detached at the position where the shot was fired.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — **Source follows the ship (Wave Laser).** During the Wave Laser beam's visible lifetime, its rendered source end re-anchors each frame to the ship's current position, so the beam stays visibly connected to the ship as it moves.
- AC2 — **Destination stays fixed.** The beam's far end remains at the launch-resolved destination — the first-intercept point when the ray met an entity, otherwise the full-extent endpoint — for the beam's whole visible life. The beam is never re-aimed or re-resolved: no damage is re-applied, no hit is recomputed, and the ray's damage result stays exactly as resolved at launch.
- AC3 — **Wrapped path preserved.** As the ship moves, the beam is redrawn along the **shortest wrapped path** from the ship's current position to the fixed destination (one segment per arena-edge crossing), consistent with the existing wrapped-segment geometry used by the Mining Laser beam.
- AC4 — **Duration, fade and cleanup unchanged.** The beam keeps its configured visible duration (0.3 s Wave Laser), fades and destroys identically, and never persists past its lifetime; the per-frame redraw stays cheap (a single Graphics, delta-driven, following the existing self-cleaning beam pattern).
- AC5 — **Game↔gym parity.** The re-anchoring lives in the shared VFX seam and the shared fire path (`CombatCoreScene.fireHitscanBeam`), so `PlayScene` and every gym render the identical tracking beam; the duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` still passes.
- AC6 — **Mining Laser re-anchors too.** The Mining Laser beam re-anchors its source the same way: each frame its source end tracks the ship's current position while its destination (the target asteroid's position **frozen at fire time**) stays fixed; the change must not regress the Mining Laser's damage, target selection or cadence (`CombatScene.onMiningLaserFire` still damages the selected live asteroid exactly once per shot, and the beam does **not** track the asteroid as it drifts).
- AC7 — **Tests and documentation.** Unit tests cover: a moving ship re-anchors the beam source while the destination never moves; no re-hit or re-damage occurs during the beam's life; the wrapped path updates when the ship crosses an arena edge mid-beam; and game↔gym parity. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (e.g. `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` only if a divergence is retained). The full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

As a player, the Wave Laser (and Mining Laser) beam now visibly emanates from your ship and stays attached as you fly, instead of floating in the space your ship occupied a moment ago.

## Constraints

- **Visual-only change.** Aim (per-shot RNG bias), cadence, damage and hit resolution are already settled at launch and must not change; the beam never re-hits or re-damages.
- **Shared seam.** The behaviour must live once in `src/scenes/core/` + `src/vfx/` so the game and every gym (GymWeapons, GymMinerals) run the same code — per the gym↔game parity convention (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).
- **Cheap by construction.** The Mining Laser fires up to once per sixteenth note (~0.1875 s); a per-frame redraw must not accumulate Graphics objects or tweens and must clean itself up on expiry and scene shutdown.
- **Ship reference lifecycle.** The beam outlives the launch frame; it must resolve the ship's position through a safe provider that survives the ship being destroyed or the scene shutting down mid-beam.

## Existing state

- **Wave Laser** is an **instant hitscan ray** (AH-0MVREBUJ5004HDRQ): `CombatCoreScene.fireHitscanBeam` resolves the ray once at launch (`resolveHitscanRay` in `src/scenes/core/hitscanBeam.ts`), applies exactly 1 damage at the first intercept through the shared kill seam, and renders the static polyline with `spawnHitscanBeam` (`src/vfx/hitscanBeam.ts`) — a red column with white-hot core, faded via a 0.3 s tween. The beam geometry is frozen at the launch muzzle position.
- **Mining Laser** fires an instant beam from the ship to the selected asteroid: `CombatScene.onMiningLaserFire` calls `spawnMiningLaserBeam` (`src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.ts`), which draws a static wrapped polyline from the **fire-time** ship position to the **fire-time** target position and ages it over 0.12 s via a delta-driven update. This module already owns the wrapped shortest-path helper (`miningLaserBeamSegments`) that the anchored beam would share.
- Both beams are therefore disconnected from the ship for the rest of their visible life once the ship moves — exactly the reported defect.

## Desired change

- Extend the beam VFX seam with an **anchored-beam renderer**: instead of drawing a one-shot static polyline, the beam Graphics takes a **source provider** (a function returning the ship's current position, or a scene method like `getPlayer()`) plus a **fixed destination** point, and on each frame recomputes the wrapped shortest path (`miningLaserBeamSegments`-style, from `src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.ts`) between the current source and the fixed destination, clearing and redrawing the Graphics. Duration, fade, registry and shutdown cleanup stay as today.
- `CombatCoreScene.fireHitscanBeam` passes the player as the source anchor and `resolution.end` as the fixed destination (the intercept point, or the full-extent endpoint when nothing was intercepted).
- `CombatScene.onMiningLaserFire` snapshots the target position at fire time (freezing the destination — the beam does **not** track the asteroid as it drifts, per "destination stays fixed") and passes the player as the source anchor.

## Key Files:

- `src/vfx/hitscanBeam.ts` — Wave Laser beam VFX: replace the static-polyline draw with the per-frame source-following anchored render (source provider + fixed destination), keeping duration/fade/registry semantics.
- `src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.ts` — home of the wrapped shortest-path helper (`miningLaserBeamSegments`) the anchored beam reuses; Mining Laser beam gets the same treatment (confirmed in scope, Q1 = A).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `fireHitscanBeam`: pass the player anchor + `resolution.end` to the renderer.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — `onMiningLaserFire`: freeze the target position at fire time and pass the player anchor.
- `src/scenes/core/hitscanBeam.ts` — ray geometry (unchanged; supplies the fixed destination via the existing `resolution.end`).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — parity guard that must still pass unchanged.
- Tests (new/updated): `src/vfx/hitscanBeam.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts`, `src/vfx/miningLaserBeam.test.ts`, plus any gym test that exercises the beam while the ship moves.

## Related work

- AH-0MVREBUJ5004HDRQ (completed, v0.1.18) — **Wave laser redesign**: built the hitscan beam seam (`src/scenes/core/hitscanBeam.ts`, `src/vfx/hitscanBeam.ts`) that this item now makes ship-tracking.
- AH-0MW9QMP2P0032BWW (completed, v0.1.21) — **Shared core mining-laser fire step**: the shared `CombatCoreScene._updateMiningLaser` / `CombatScene.onMiningLaserFire` fire path the Mining Laser change would extend.
- AH-0MW9QMQ7B005WFH9 (completed, v0.1.21) — **Mining-laser beam VFX and audio cue**: the `spawnMiningLaserBeam` renderer and its wrapped-segment helper.
- AH-0MW9QMSI7005UU9P (completed) — **Gym coverage and parity for the mining laser** (GymMinerals), the parity gym for the Mining Laser half.
- AH-0MW10J31B0053E56 (completed) — **Wave Laser tuning**: level-resolved ray length/aim bias that fixes the level-0 length at 240 px.
- AH-0MV5DFBVW002J2XO (completed) — **Orbital Fires in direction of orb**: precedent for re-anchoring a fired effect's origin to a moving source object.

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — Beam pivot feel.** With a near intercept and the ship moving fast, the re-anchored beam pivots noticeably around its fixed destination, which may look unusual up close. Mitigation: source-anchor to the ship's natural firing point (the same position the ray resolved from); verify feel in the weapons gym before review.
- **R2 — Per-frame redraw cost.** The Mining Laser can fire every ~0.1875 s; a per-frame beam redraw must stay a single Graphics redraw with no object or tween accumulation. Mitigation: reuse the existing delta-driven, self-cleaning beam lifecycle and clear/redraw in place.
- **R3 — Ship destroyed mid-beam.** The beam outlives the launch frame, so the source provider must be safe if the ship is destroyed or the scene shuts down mid-life. Mitigation: provider guards against a missing player plus the existing shutdown cleanup.
- **R4 — Scope creep.** Re-aiming the beam at a moving enemy, tracking moving destinations, applying source-tracking to other weapons, or touching damage/aim/cadence are **out of scope**; any such opportunity should be recorded as a linked work item, not added to this change.

## Assumptions

- **A1 — Visual-only.** The beam's source tracking is a rendering change; the ray still resolves once at launch and damage, aim and cadence are untouched. Re-resolution or re-hits would contradict "destination stays fixed" and are out of scope.
- **A2 — Destination frozen at launch.** The beam's far end is the launch-resolved end point (first-intercept point, or full-extent endpoint) and stays there for the beam's whole visible life, even if the intercepted entity or anything else moves.
- **A3 — Mining Laser in scope** (confirmed by the producer: Q1 = A). The Mining Laser beam's destination is frozen at fire time — it does **not** follow the asteroid as it drifts; only the source re-anchors to the ship.

## Open Questions

- **RESOLVED Q1 — Is the Mining Laser in scope?** Producer answer: **A — yes, include the Mining Laser.** The Mining Laser beam has the identical static-polyline defect (0.12 s visible, ship up to ~21 px clear), and once the anchored-beam renderer exists the incremental cost is small. AC6 now mandates the same source-follows-ship treatment with the destination frozen at fire time.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-16 — Intake draft created from the seed description (auto-dispatched). Scope, ACs, key files and the single open scope question (Q1) recorded; duplicate check performed (no overlapping item found).
- 2026-11-16 — Producer answered Q1 = **A (Mining Laser in scope)**. AC6 rewritten as a firm criterion (destination frozen at fire time, no asteroid-tracking), headline/desired-change/key-files updated, the Open Question marked RESOLVED, and the Appendix records the answer.
- 2026-11-16 — Plan auto-complete (plan skill, Process step 1): the item is a bug (not an epic) whose description already carries measurable ACs (AC1–AC7) and a minimal implementation sketch (anchored-beam renderer + source provider + fixed destination, key files, constraints, risks). Effort Small / risk Medium just misses the auto-skip threshold (which requires risk Low), so the plan pre-check routed to the Process — but planning adds no value here; no decomposition into child features. AC-coverage review: `proceed` (no children, no conflicts). Decision recorded; item advanced to `plan_complete`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (asked as part of this intake): "Is the Mining Laser in scope for the source-follows-ship beam change?" — Answer (producer, 2026-11-16): **A — yes, include the Mining Laser.** Final: A (Option A — include), as recommended. Source: producer reply to the handoff comment AH-C0MWJAAJH80067EGM on the work item; research: both beams render a static polyline frozen at fire time and visibly detach from the ship (Wave Laser 0.3 s visible / ~50 px at max speed; Mining Laser 0.12 s / ~21 px), and one shared anchored-beam renderer covers both.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTV7OAJM002GGMM** – Move control buttons for gym scenes to the bottom (completed)
- **AH-0MUZMTS8J0029FSS** – Add figure-of-8 boss movement in shared core (completed)
- **AH-0MV1EDVNF004MTYN** – Wave laser audio fire/pickup cues and leveling-gym round-robin (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: destination, fires, fixed, laser, mining, move, moves, needs, origin, point, possibly, ship, source, stays, wave
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: destination, fires, fixed, laser, mining, move, moves, needs, origin, point, ship, source, stays, wave
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: destination, fires, fixed, laser, mining, move, moves, needs, origin, point, ship, source, stays, wave

# Test runner crashes with UnboundLocalError when a full-scope suite resolves to no commands

## Problem Statement

`run_tests.py` crashes with `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'state_changed_flag'` when a named suite resolves to zero commands. Instead of reporting the empty resolution gracefully, the function references a variable that was never bound.

## Users

- Agent sessions that run the test skill with a named suite (e.g. `--suite node`) that happens to resolve to no commands in the current repo.
- CI / automation that invokes the test runner with varying suites across repositories.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A full-scope run whose suite resolves to no commands completes without an `UnboundLocalError` — either with an actionable message naming the suite and resolution path, or a clean early return with a zero-command report.
2. The `state_changed_flag` variable is initialised before the command-execution loop (or the loop body guard handles the empty case), so the post-loop aggregation path never touches an unbound variable.
3. A regression test exercises the zero-command path (mocking `commands` to an empty list, or using a suite name that resolves to nothing) and asserts no crash.

## Impact

Users running the test runner against a suite with zero commands get a clear, actionable error message instead of an obscure Python `UnboundLocalError` crash.

## Constraints

- Fix is in a shared skill (`run_tests.py` in the `test` skill scripts); changes must not break existing callers.
- The existing `state_changed_flag` semantics (mid-run checkout movement tracking) must be preserved for the normal non-empty command path.

## Existing State

`run_tests.py` initialises `state_changed_flag` inside the `for cmd in commands:` loop body (line 3188). After the loop, the function reads `state_changed_flag` on line 3281 to populate `state_changed_during_run` in the result dict. When `commands` is empty, the loop body never executes, leaving the name unbound.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Move `state_changed_flag` initialisation before the `for cmd in commands:` loop (line ~3183, after `slot_waits`).
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/tests/` — Add regression test for the zero-command path.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep:** The fix is narrowly scoped to the `UnboundLocalError`. Do not refactor other loop-scoped variables (e.g. `command_waits`, `command_elapsed`) unless they show the same pattern.
- **Assumption:** Moving the initialisation before the loop is safe — `state_changed_flag` is reset per-command inside the loop for the normal case. We should verify whether a per-iteration reset is actually needed or whether a single pre-loop initialisation suffices.
- **Risk:** If `state_changed_flag` is intentionally per-command (reset for each iteration), a single pre-loop initialisation may lose the reset semantics. The fix should preserve per-command reset only if the logic requires it; otherwise the pre-loop init is sufficient.

## Related Work

- Discovered from AH-0MWJ1680Z001QYV2 ("Bot oscillates too much") — the agent was running the test skill during implementation and hit this crash.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Does `state_changed_flag` need per-command reset, or is a single pre-loop initialisation sufficient?" — Answer (Map): A pre-loop initialisation to `None` is sufficient. The per-command reassignment on line 3224 (`state_changed_flag = run.get("state_changed_during_run")`) overwrites the value each iteration; the post-loop read (line 3281) captures the last iteration's value (or `None` if zero iterations). The bug is simply that the declaration line never runs when the loop body is skipped.

# Intake brief — Hex Map Information UX (AH-0MWL4QCVD007WOAM)

## Headline

The Hex Map screen (`HexMapScene`) draws roughly fifteen separately positioned
text objects and a ring of tiles with **no sectioning at all**: war status,
transient "what just happened" news, the map itself, the selected hex's intel and
the controls legend all float over the same background, in three different
columns and two different font conventions. This item introduces named,
visually bounded **sections** — each with its own heading — so every group of
information is distinguishable at a glance.

## Problem statement

There is a lot of information on the Hex Map and too little structure holding it
apart. Measured against the shipped renderer (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`,
960×540), the screen currently carries:

| What is drawn | Where it sits today |
|---|---|
| Screen title, and the run result line (`RUN: VICTORY · score N`) | centred, top (`y=18`, `y=46`) |
| Ring progress (`RING 2 — 3/12 HEXES HELD`) | left column (`x=24`, `y=62`) |
| Frontier strength (`FRONTIER · STR n · BEAT ≤ m (k IN REACH)`) | left column (`y=82`) |
| Hangar fleet + bank (`HANGAR · hull · n min · n cores`) | left column (`y=102`) |
| `ATTACK — FOCUSED HEX` panel (rolled-in defence report) | left column (`y=118`, conditional) |
| `HANGAR ASSAULT` banner (ring won / hangar falls) | left column (`y=300`, conditional) |
| `◀ HANGAR` action row | left column (`y=468`) |
| `READ THE MAP` legend, six lines of static help | right column (`y=112`–`y=182`) |
| `SELECTED HEX — FULL INTEL` detail panel | right column (`y=200`) |
| Hex tiles (`AGG n` + ownership marker + `(q,r)`), attack arrows, hangar marker | centre |
| Keyboard hint line | bottom centre (`y=530`) |

Three problems follow from that inventory:

1. **Unlike information is adjacent, like information is apart.** The three
   left-hand header lines mix ring progress, frontier combat maths and hangar
   inventory with no heading to separate them, while the two halves of "the
   selected hex" (its intel, right column; its attack row, left column) sit on
   opposite sides of the screen.
2. **Transient news has no home.** The run result is centred at the top, the
   hangar-assault outcome is a left-hand banner, and the banked win-bonus line
   (`model.winBonusLine`) is computed but **never drawn at all** — its only
   consumer is the `getWinBonusLine()` test seam. "What just happened" therefore
   arrives in up to three different places, one of which is nowhere.
3. **Help competes with content.** A six-line static legend occupies the top of
   the same right-hand column as the dynamic intel panel it explains, so the
   loudest text in that column is documentation rather than information about
   the player's war.

## Users

- **The Hangar War player** landing on the map between sorties.
  - *As a player, I want the map's status, my last sortie's outcome, the ring
    itself and the selected hex's intel each in their own labelled section, so I
    can find one thing without reading everything.*
  - *As a player, I want to know what just happened (victory/defeat, ring won or
    hangar falls, minerals banked) in one place, so I do not have to hunt three
    corners of the screen for the aftermath of my deployment.*
  - *As a player reading the selected hex, I want its intel and its attack row
    together, so one hex is one story rather than two panels apart.*
  - *As a colour-blind player, I want sections distinguished by headings and
    framing rather than by colour alone, consistent with the map's existing
    CVD-safe conventions.*
- **The maintainer** of the shared `buildHexMapModel` → `renderHexMap` pair,
  who needs the section layout to live in one renderer so the game and the
  `GymHexWar` parity gym cannot drift (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).

## Producer decisions (2026-11-17)

- **Q1 = (a)** — sections are **bordered, headed panels** laid out in fixed
  columns; every section has a frame, a heading and a bounded rect.
- **Q2 = (b)** — **four content sections plus a controls footer**: WAR STATUS,
  LAST SORTIE, MAP, SELECTED HEX (intel **and** its attack row together), and
  CONTROLS/LEGEND.
- **Q3 = (a)** — the banked win-bonus line **is rendered**, inside LAST SORTIE.

## Section model (producer-approved)

Four content sections plus a controls footer, each drawn as a **bordered,
headed panel** with a bounded rect:

| Section | Contains | Visibility |
|---|---|---|
| `war-status` | ring progress, frontier strength / beatable ceiling / in-reach count, hangar hull + banked minerals/cores | always |
| `last-sortie` | run result line, banked win bonus, hangar-assault outcome (`RING WON…` / `HANGAR FALLS…`) | only when the landing carries one of those |
| `map` | the ring tiles, attack arrows and hangar marker | always |
| `selected-hex` | the focused hex's full intel **and** its `ATTACK — FOCUSED HEX` row | always (panel body may be empty when nothing is focused) |
| `controls` | keyboard hint line + the `READ THE MAP` legend | always |

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Section registry on the shared view.** `HexMapView` publishes a `sections`
  list — `{ key, heading, rect }` per rendered section — and every rendered text
  object, tile and arrow lies inside **exactly one** section rect, with no two
  section rects overlapping and every rect inside the 960×540 frame.
- **Every section is a bordered, headed panel (Q1 = a).** Each of `war-status`,
  `last-sortie` (when shown), `map`, `selected-hex` and `controls` draws a panel
  frame and one heading from a shared exported constant (`WAR STATUS`,
  `LAST SORTIE`, `SELECTED HEX`, `CONTROLS`, and the map's own title), in one
  consistent style and position convention, so the groupings are distinguishable
  without relying on colour.
- **No information is lost.** Every string the current renderer draws still
  renders, in its new section; the tile labels (`AGG n`, ownership marker,
  `(q,r)`), arrows, hint line and legend text are unchanged in content.
- **Transient news is grouped and complete (Q2 = b, Q3 = a).** The run result
  line, the hangar-assault banner and the banked win-bonus line
  (`WIN BONUS BANKED: +N MINERALS`, from `model.winBonusLine`) render **only**
  inside `last-sortie`; the win-bonus line is now actually drawn, not merely
  queryable. When the landing carries none of the three, the section is absent
  (no empty headed box).
- **One hex, one section.** The selected hex's intel and its attack row render
  inside the same `selected-hex` section; the attack row is hidden (not moved to
  another section) when the focused hex is in no attack.
- **Help no longer competes with content.** The `READ THE MAP` legend moves into
  the `controls` section and no longer occupies the intel column.
- **Legibility at 960×540.** No section body text overdraws a hex tile or the
  hangar marker; long strings (draw name, assault arithmetic) word-wrap inside
  their section; no rendered text is smaller than today's smallest (9px) and
  headings are at least 10px.
- **Game/gym parity, one shared layout.** All layout lives in
  `renderHexMap`/`hexMap.ts`; `GymHexWar` renders the same sections read-only
  through the same call, and no gym-local or scene-local layout exists (the
  existing `renderHexMap` equivalence assertions stay green).
- **Interaction contract unchanged.** Grid arrow navigation, Tab/Shift+Tab
  cycling, Enter/Space inspect-or-deploy, tile hover/click, the `◀ HANGAR` row
  and ESC-to-menu behave exactly as before; the attract traversal still takes
  exactly one next action and cannot stall on a section.
- **Regression coverage.** `HexMapScene.test.ts`, the renderer/`hexIntel` tests
  and `GymHexWar.test.ts` pin the section registry (keys, headings, non-overlap,
  in-frame), `last-sortie` visibility toggling, and that the selected-hex intel
  and attack row share a section; position-only pins may be updated, behaviour
  pins may not be weakened.
- **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries** — GDD §8.2 (the
  map's screen surface), the `hexMap.ts` module docblock, and
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` if its row description changes.
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A Hangar War player can read the map at a glance: the war's status, the last
sortie's outcome, the ring itself, the selected hex's intel and the controls each
sit in their own labelled section instead of scattering across three columns.

## Constraints

- **Renderer-only change.** The model (`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`) stays
  the single source of every string; `hexMap.ts` only draws and positions. No
  gameplay rule, resolver call or persisted state is added.
- **One layout for game and gym.** The gym↔game parity contract and the existing
  `renderHexMap` equivalence assertions forbid a second layout implementation.
- **Single 960×540 viewport.** No scrolling, panning, tabs or collapsible
  sections unless the producer chooses the tabbed option in Q1.
- **Transient launch data stays transient** — run result, tick record, assault
  and win bonus are never persisted; a later entry renders no `last-sortie`.
- **Existing CVD-safe conventions hold** — section distinction must not depend on
  colour; the tile ownership encoding (blue/orange + filled/hollow marker) is
  untouched.
- **No new assets or fonts** — monospace text and Phaser Graphics panels only.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` (951 lines) holds every layout constant
  (`PANEL_X`, `ATTACK_PANEL_Y`, `ASSAULT_BANNER_Y`, legend rows, hint line) and
  draws all of the inventory above. There is no section abstraction: each text
  object is positioned by a hand-tuned literal.
- `HexMapView` already exposes behavioural seams (`getRows`, `getArrows`,
  `getPanelText`, `getLeftPanelText`, `getAssaultText`, …) but nothing describing
  screen regions, so no test can currently assert grouping or non-overlap.
- `model.winBonusLine` exists (`src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` →
  `defenceReport.ts`) and is surfaced only by `HexMapScene.getWinBonusLine()`;
  the renderer never draws it.
- Prior work already fixed the map's *readability* (reveal filter, CVD-safe tiles,
  coordinates, titled detail-panel lines) and its *navigation* (grid arrows), so
  this item is the remaining structural/visual-hierarchy step.

## Desired change

A sectioned Hex Map: a small number of named, bounded regions with headings, each
holding one kind of information, drawn by the shared renderer so the game and the
parity gym stay identical; transient sortie news gathered into one place; the
selected hex's intel and attack row brought together; help demoted to a controls
footer.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — the whole layout: section rects, headings,
  legend relocation, last-sortie grouping; add `sections` to `HexMapView`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` — shared section-heading constants and any
  model wiring for the last-sortie lines (`winBonusLine` is already published)
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — query seam for `sections`, transient launch data
  plumbing (no rule change)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — renders the same sections read-only

# Anomaly (elite) enemies and wave twists

Discovered from: the 2026-11-17 gameplay-mechanics review (rank 7 of 10; direction: create, **Medium** priority).

## Goal (user story)

As a player working through the campaign's waves, I want some waves to field a
visibly special enemy with an extra behaviour and a real reward, so that wave 60
does not feel like wave 6 with more bodies.

## Problem statement

The campaign is 100 waves (ten per level) built from a fixed archetype roster
with escalating counts, and difficulty rises on exactly two axes — enemy count
(1.00× → 2.00×) and a falling per-kill drop chance (GDD §4.6). After the
classic-arcade debut in level 6, novelty is carried almost entirely by density,
so later waves read as the same formations scaled up.

Evidence of the gap:

- No elite, anomaly, champion or variant identifier exists in `src/` today.
- Archetypes are already per-enemy CSV data (`src/data/enemy-configs.csv`) with
  `movementClass`/`attackClass`, so a variant axis is a data change on an
  existing spawn path.
- The bounded-behaviour precedent already exists: the hex personalities
  implement exactly two shared combat mechanics (a projectile-slowing `nebula`
  and a reinforcement-summoning `summoner`) once in the shared combat core
  (`src/scenes/core/hexPersonalityMechanics.ts`), proving the pattern is cheap.

## The mechanic (full proposal)

1. **One elite per wave, authored or seeded.** A wave may author one **elite**
   spawn; when a wave authors none, a seeded budget grants an elite on a
   tunable share of waves (initial `ELITE_WAVE_CHANCE = 0.15`). **Level 1 never
   spawns an elite** — onboarding and the experience-target baseline stay
   untouched.
2. **A variant of a counted archetype, never a new entity.** An elite is the
   same archetype with: a distinct aura + rim treatment (visibly different
   silhouette treatment, not colour alone), `+ELITE_BONUS_HP` (1–3, data-driven
   per archetype) and **one** extra behaviour drawn from a small bounded set:
   - **splitter** — on death it releases two ordinary children of its own
     archetype (reusing the shared spawn seam the asteroid/harvester spawners
     use);
   - **reinforced** — it spawns behind the shipped force-field layer at one
     extra field hit (reusing `enemyForceFieldHits` and the shared bubble
     visuals);
   - **volatile** — on death it leaves a short-lived radial burst of its own
     bullets (reusing the boss pulse/minion vocabulary and the existing enemy
     bullet seam).
3. **Wave accounting is unchanged.** An elite is a counted wave enemy, so a wave
   still clears only when its ships are destroyed; it is never an asteroid-style
   non-counted hazard and can never stall or short-circuit a wave.
4. **A real, visible reward.** An elite always drops from the shared pool and
   carries a guaranteed **mineral bump** (2–4, level-scaled through the existing
   `levelScaling` curve). Its drop is announced by a distinct death cue so the
   payoff is legible at a glance.
5. **Announced, never a surprise.** The wave's opening cue names the elite and a
   short-lived `ELITE` tag tracks the hull while it lives, so the player can
   prioritise it — this is the decision the mechanic exists to create.
6. **Arcade-safe.** Elites are authored/off by default in the arcade campaign's
   first fields until the bot batch clears (see AC9); the hex ring's boss
   deployments are unaffected (no elite spawns there).

## Why this improves player enjoyment

- It adds cheap novelty exactly where the game is most repetitive, at the
  moment-to-moment scale the player feels most often.
- A priority target makes a familiar formation a decision again: "kill the
  splitter first or lose the gap".
- The guaranteed reward gives a wave-clear plan a visible payoff, improving the
  mineral cadence that the middle loop depends on.

## Acceptance criteria

1. An elite variant is data-driven (CSV/config column plus a bounded behaviour
   id), validated loudly: an unknown behaviour id or an elite on an uncounted
   hazard fails at load, not at spawn.
2. Level 1 never spawns an elite; a wave that authors one spawns exactly one;
   the seeded budget path is deterministic given the run seed.
3. An elite is a counted wave enemy: the wave clears only when it is destroyed,
   it survives the wave-timeout carry-over rule exactly as an ordinary enemy,
   and it can never be an `asteroid`/`lane-traffic` non-counted hazard.
4. Each of the three behaviours works through a shared seam (no bespoke
   per-archetype copy): children spawn through the shared spawn path, the extra
   field hit through `enemyForceFieldHits`, the death burst through the shared
   enemy-bullet seam; a behaviour absent from the data reproduces today's
   behaviour byte-for-byte.
5. Reward: an elite always drops from the shared pool and pays the level-scaled
   guaranteed mineral bump, with a distinct death cue that respects the shared
   SFX settings.
6. Legibility: the elite's aura, tag and opening-wave announcement read without
   relying on colour alone; the tag disappears exactly when the elite dies.
7. Gym↔game parity: `GymFodderEnemies` (or the level gym) spawns every elite
   behaviour through the same code path as the game, with a `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`
   row.
8. Determinism: same seed + same wave ⇒ same elite, same position, same reward
   (the seeded budget consumes the run-seeded stream in a documented order, and
   the campaign variety/signature audit is unaffected because an elite does not
   change an archetype *set*).
9. Balance evidence: a same-seed bot batch shows `survivalSeconds`,
   `mineralsCollected` and `avoidableHits` inside the experience-target bands;
   the level-scaling table in `docs/BALANCING.md` is re-measured with elites on
   and the result recorded on this item before the shipped default is raised
   above zero.
10. Documentation: GDD §4.1/§4.6 and the new §8.3 entry, plus `docs/BALANCING.md`
    with the measured before/after.
11. The full project test suite passes (through the test skill).

## Impact

A player clearing a familiar formation now spots a lit, tougher anomaly with a
guaranteed payoff and has to decide whether to break formation to kill it first,
so mid-campaign waves carry a decision instead of only more bodies.

## Constraints and assumptions

- **Bounded content.** Three behaviours maximum for the first slice; each is a
  re-use of a shipped seam, and none may need a new entity class.
- **Ships only.** Elites are variants of counted archetypes, never hazards, so
  wave-completion logic and the sequencer's clearability invariant are
  untouched.
- **Onboarding frozen.** Level 1 is elite-free and the level-1 identity
  transform is preserved.
- **No new persistence.** Elite choice is derived from the run seed and the wave
  data; nothing is written to any save.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` + `src/core/configTypes.ts` — the variant columns
  (`eliteBehaviour`, `eliteBonusHp`).
- `src/waves/` (planner) — the seeded elite budget and per-wave authoring.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` spawn path, `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — aura/tag
  and the death behaviour hook.
- `src/scenes/core/hexPersonalityMechanics.ts` — the precedent seam to mirror
  for a bounded shared-mechanic set.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts` — parity row.
- `docs/BALANCING.md`, GDD §4.1, §4.6, §8.3.

## Related work

- GDD §4.1 (archetypes and force fields), §4.2 (wave structures and the
  wave-timeout carry-over rule), §4.6 (the two difficulty axes).
- Hex variety: personalities, contracts and ring landmarks (AH-0MVWZYQN8007SXIG)
  — the shipped bounded-mechanics precedent.
- Enemy roster docs guard (`src/enemyRosterDocs.test.ts`) — the variant axis
  must be added to the roster documentation it validates.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- **AH-0MUE2MGM0001XEH9** – CSV seed data files (enemy-configs.csv, ship-config.csv) (completed)

# Bot selection of upgrades are slower

## Problem statement

When the attract/demo bot is presented with the hold-full upgrade selection
overlay it picks an option after only **900 ms** (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`),
so a viewer has no real chance to read the three offers before the bot has
already chosen — and once it chooses, the choice screen is torn down and only
the 3-2-1 countdown numeral remains, so nothing on screen says **which** item
the bot took. The bot's upgrade picks should dwell long enough to be watched
and should be visible on the countdown.

## Users

- **Attract/demo viewer** (the player watching the menu's 👁 Watch Demo
  attract run, or an idle-menu session): *"As a viewer of attract mode, I want
  to see the bot's upgrade options for a couple of seconds and then see which
  one it picked while the countdown plays, so the demo reads as a deliberate
  choice rather than an instant flicker."*
- **Player (human selection, incidental):** *"As a player, once I choose an
  upgrade I want to be reminded which one I took while the 3-2-1 countdown
  runs."* — the shared overlay tears its choice UI down on selection, so the
  chosen title is the only record during the countdown.
- **Designer / producer:** *"As a designer, I want the bot's overlay dwell to
  be one named, tunable constant so I can pace the demo without hunting magic
  numbers."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — **Bot dwell is 2.5 s.** In demo/attract mode the hold-full upgrade
  selection overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`) auto-selects only after a **2500 ms**
  pause, sourced from one named constant (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` in
  `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`, raised from 900); the bot therefore visibly shows
  the offered upgrades before choosing. Normal (non-demo) play still waits for a
  real pointer/keyboard selection and never auto-selects.
- AC2 — **Selected title under the countdown.** From the moment an option is
  selected until the countdown completes, the overlay renders the **chosen
  option's title** (its catalogue name, e.g. `Spread Shot Lv.3`) beneath the
  large 3-2-1 countdown numeral, and the title text is **destroyed** when the
  countdown finishes and the overlay closes — no title text, text object or
  tween outlives the overlay, and a fresh hold-full starts with no stale title.
- AC3 — **Countdown and resume are unchanged.** The selection still drives the
  existing beat-locked 3-2-1 countdown (2250 ms at the default 80 BPM) with its
  rising cue, the reduced-volume ghost fire still runs underneath, and the
  choice is still applied on the beat after "1" with the launcher's beat clock
  re-based. The title is purely additive presentation and never delays or
  alters selection, application or resume timing.
- AC4 — **Scope contained.** The mini-boss reward wheel's demo auto-spin delay
  is **not** changed by AC1 (it keeps its current separate delay/constant), and
  no other surface's timing changes; every gym that launches the shared overlay
  keeps its existing behaviour (no `autoSelectMs` passed) apart from gaining the
  title readout.
- AC5 — **Tests.** Unit tests in `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts`
  cover: the chosen title is exposed and rendered while the countdown runs, and
  is gone (`null`) after the countdown completes; a manual selection shows its
  own title; the constant-pinned bot dwell is asserted (auto-select does not
  fire before 2500 ms and does fire after it). The demo integration test
  (`src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`) still asserts the
  selection → countdown → resume path and asserts the selected title is visible
  during the countdown. All existing overlay, gym-parity and countdown tests
  stay green.
- AC6 — **Docs.** `README.md` (attract/demo mode section) and
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 auto-select bullet and §4.5
  beat-locked-countdown bullet) are updated to state the **2.5 s** bot dwell
  and the selected title shown under the countdown (and removed with it).
- AC7 — **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries.**
- AC8 — **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A viewer of the attract-mode demo now gets a clear 2.5-second look at the bot's
three upgrade offers and can see exactly which one it took while the countdown
plays, instead of a near-instant pick that left no trace of the choice.

## Constraints

- Demo-only for the dwell: normal play must not gain any auto-selection
  (existing AC5 of AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB must stay true).
- Tunables live in one shared place (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`), never as
  scattered magic numbers.
- The overlay keeps its single `onSelect` contract; it must not reach back into
  `PlayScene` by scene key.
- The countdown stays beat-derived (`createHoldFullCountdown` /
  `beatPeriodMs`), never a hard-coded 2250 ms.
- Headless test harnesses collapse text metrics to 0, so any title layout must
  keep a measurable fallback (mirroring the existing `CHOICE_*_LINE_HEIGHT`
  constants) and stay inside the 960 × 720 playfield.
- The overlay is shared by `PlayScene`, `HexMapScene`, `GymFormationScene`,
  `GymWeaponLeveling` and `GymPowerUpLeveling`; the title addition must keep
  gym↔game parity (no per-scene copies).

## Existing state

- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` exports `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS = 900` — the
  demo dwell used for the hold-full choice auto-select, the mini-boss
  hold-full-style fallback choice, **and** the mini-boss wheel auto-spin
  (`PlayScene.openMiniBossReward` → `autoSpinMs`).
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` (`init` → `autoSelectMs` /
  `autoSelectIndex`, `create` → `this.time.delayedCall`) auto-selects on the
  demo path. `select(index)` records the pending selection, tears down the
  whole choice UI (backdrop, heading, option labels/descriptions/details, the
  `★ New` badges, the `YOUR UPGRADES` panel, the keydown handler) and draws the
  large countdown numeral at `COUNTDOWN_Y = 270` (96 px, neon cyan).
  `completeSelection()` destroys the numeral, invokes `onSelect` and stops the
  scene. Public accessors already exist: `getCountdownText()`,
  `isCountdownActive()`, `isChoiceScreenVisible()`, `getOverlayElapsedMs()`.
- `src/scenes/core/holdFullCountdown.ts` owns the pure 3-2-1 scheduler
  (`HOLD_FULL_COUNTDOWN_COUNTS = 3`, `HOLD_FULL_COUNTDOWN_DURATION_MS`).
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` uses its own `demoDwellMs ?? HANGAR_WAR_TRAVERSAL_DWELL_MS`
  for demo reward overlays, so it does not depend on the bot choice constant.
- Docs pin the current 900 ms pace: `README.md` (attract/demo paragraph) and
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 ("**900 ms**") and §4.5 (countdown tears
  the choice screen down, "leaving only the countdown numeral").
- Tests reference the constant symbolically (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`), so
  a value change flows through `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` and
  `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` waits without hard-coded numbers.

## Desired change

1. Raise the demo dwell to 2500 ms (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`), keeping the
   mini-boss wheel's demo spin delay at its current pace via a separate constant
   so only the upgrade-selection pause slows.
2. In `MineralChoiceScene`, render the chosen option's title beneath the
   countdown numeral when a selection starts the countdown, expose it for tests
   (e.g. `getCountdownTitle()`), and destroy it alongside the numeral in
   `completeSelection()` (and defensively on shutdown).
3. Update the overlay's module doc comment, README and GDD to describe the
   2.5 s bot dwell and the title-under-countdown readout.
4. Cover the above with unit tests and keep the demo integration and gym-parity
   suites green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — raise `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` to 2500 and
  (if the wheel is scoped out) add a separate demo-spin delay constant; update
  the doc comment.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — new countdown-title text object + layout
  constant, title creation in `select()`, destruction in `completeSelection()`
  and shutdown, `getCountdownTitle()` accessor, module doc comment.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — hold-full/mini-boss-fallback `autoSelectMs` wiring
  and the wheel `autoSpinMs` constant separation (comments mention the new
  pace).
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — title-visible/title-cleared
  and 2500 ms dwell tests.
- `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` — assert the selected title under
  the countdown on the demo path.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — only where the wheel/choice delay is asserted.
- `README.md` — attract/demo paragraph: 2.5 s dwell + selected title.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 auto-select bullet, §4.5 countdown
  bullet.

## Related work

- AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB — *Demo bot: human-like input limits and complete the
  hold-full upgrade choice* (completed): introduced the demo auto-select and
  `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`.
- AH-0MV55OBKS006TL4N — *Demo/attract auto-select routes through the countdown*
  (completed): the bot's auto-select must drive the same selection → 3-2-1 →
  on-beat resume path.
- AH-0MV55OAQT004NMSN — *Beat-locked 3-2-1 countdown and on-beat resume*
  (completed): owns the countdown scheduler and the "numeral only" teardown this
  item extends with the chosen title.
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F — *AI bot does not know how to select upgrade in
  mini-boss reward screen* (completed): the mini-boss reward auto-select and
  wheel spin sharing the same demo delay.
- AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q — *Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the
  ship's hold and grant a power-up choice* (completed): the hold-full overlay
  itself.
- AH-0MV722WJS0075UTZ — countdown teardown of the choice UI (the behaviour the
  title readout complements).
- AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4 / AH-0MW3MLV2V001NWBR — the retired Extra Life
  auto-select preference; the auto-select always takes option 0 today.

### Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z** – Some power-ups appear to do nothing (completed)
- **AH-0MV55OBKS006TL4N** – Demo/attract auto-select routes through the
  countdown (completed)
- **AH-0MVD20MYX0028JFL** – Close coverage gap: AC2 upgrade choices simulated
  (completed)

### Potentially related docs

- `README.md` (attract/demo mode paragraph) — documents the current 900 ms
  auto-select and the countdown/resume cadence.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (bot) and §4.5 (hold-full overlay) —
  the two canonical descriptions of this behaviour.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — demo capture expectations that exercise the
  overlay.

## Assumptions and decisions for producer confirmation

- **A1 — Dwell scope.** The 2.5 s pause applies to the **upgrade selection
  overlay** only (hold-full choice, and the hold-full-style mini-boss
  fallback, which reuse `MineralChoiceScene`). The **mini-boss reward wheel**
  keeps its current demo auto-spin pace (split into its own constant), because
